Container.Name: Nexview
Container.Overview: Nexview is a self-hosted media discovery dashboard for a household - family, flatmates, a circle of friends. It shows new releases from TMDB, marks what is already in your library, and hands requests to Radarr (movies) and Sonarr (shows). Everyone gets their own account with roles, approvals, quotas, per-user blocklists and an age restriction, so children can browse a view of their own. The interface is available in English and German. Nexview downloads nothing itself and stores no media. It is the front door to a setup you already run - it does not replace any part of it. Without a TMDB key Nexview starts with sample data, so you can look around before deciding anything.
Container.Description: Nexview is a self-hosted media discovery dashboard for a household. It shows new releases from TMDB, marks what is already in your Radarr and Sonarr libraries, and turns a request into an add on the right instance with the right quality profile and root folder. Accounts and roles: every member signs in separately. Admins approve or decline, set monthly quotas per person, block genres or ratings per person, and can put an account into a children's view with large category tiles and an age filter. All data lives in a single SQLite database under /data, together with the key used to encrypt your stored Radarr, Sonarr and TMDB credentials. Back up that one folder and you have backed up Nexview. Set PUID and PGID to the user that should own the files - 99 and 100 are the Unraid defaults and work out of the box.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port you reach Nexview at. Container port: 8000

Config.Name: Data (Container Path: /data)
Config.Description: Holds the SQLite database, the encryption key for your stored API credentials, and profile pictures. Back up this folder.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id that should own the files in /data. 99 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id that should own the files in /data. 100 is the Unraid default.

Config.Name: Time Zone
Config.Description: Time zone used for the log and for dates in the interface, for example Europe/Berlin.

Config.Name: Secret Key
Config.Description: Signs login tokens and encrypts your stored Radarr, Sonarr and TMDB credentials. Leave blank: Nexview generates one on first start and keeps it in /data/secret.key.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: Emergency override: quiet, normal, detailed or trace. Leave blank - the level is set inside the app and turns itself back down after troubleshooting. Only set this if Nexview will not start at all.

Config.Name: Access Token Minutes
Config.Description: How long a sign-in stays valid before it is refreshed.

Config.Name: Refresh Token Days
Config.Description: How long someone stays signed in without entering their password again.
